core_obligations: Use the permanence lemmas to get that q is of finite presentation and flat (proof lines 4731-4734).
Reduce, via the local-complete-intersection-fibre criterion, to showing that the local rings of the fibres of Y -> S and of X -> Y are complete intersections (proof lines 4735-4738).
Take the fibre at a point s and pick x in X over y in Y, so that the situation is over the spectrum of a field (proof lines 4738-4744).
Apply Avramov's result to the flat local homomorphism O_{Y,y} -> O_{X,x} whose target is a complete intersection, concluding for both rings and hence for q and f (proof lines 4745-4751).
proof_roadmap: Finite presentation and flatness of q (proof lines 4731-4734).
Reduction to complete intersection fibres (proof lines 4735-4738).
Fibre reduction to local rings over a field (proof lines 4738-4744).
difficulty_reason: Given a commutative triangle of schemes with f : X -> Y surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation and p : X -> S syntomic, the lemma asserts that both q : Y -> S and f are syntomic (statement lines 4712-4728). The proof obtains finite presentation of q from the flat-finitely-presented permanence lemma and flatness of q from the permanence lemma for flat morphisms, then uses the criterion that syntomicity is equivalent to flatness plus finite presentation plus local complete intersection fibres to reduce to a statement about local rings; after taking the fibre at a point s and picking x over y, the ring map O_{Y,y} -> O_{X,x} is a flat local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings with the target a complete intersection, and Avramov's result yields that both O_{Y,y} and O_{X,x}/m_y O_{X,x} are complete intersections (proof lines 4730-4751). The level is H3: three separate inputs are combined and the fibre reduction to a single ring-theoretic statement is displayed.
